category: tunnel (hosted): free donation-funded VPN with no account, OpenVPN and obfs4 on 21 shared gateways

free_tier.stated: Free to use with no account: 'You just install it and run it—no configuration, no account registration.' The service is donation-funded: 'The cost for us to offer RiseupVPN is approximately $60 USD per person per year', and users are asked to donate at least that. The cheapest yearly price is therefore USD 0; the suggested donation is USD 60.
free_tier.notes: No byte or time quota is stated on the pages read, and the published service configuration marks each of its 21 gateways as 'limited': false; that flag's meaning is not documented on the pages read, so the unit unlimited is an absence of a stated quota, not a vendor promise.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes
retention.notes: The vendor states it does not log the user's IP address; no stored-object retention applies.

egress.terms: No byte cap or rate is stated on the pages read. All 21 gateways in the published service configuration carry 'limited': false. The help page says RiseupVPN 'bypasses these restrictions and, because you get your own IP, makes p2p applications work much better'.
egress.free_allowance: free to use; no quota stated

interface_detail: A tunnel with desktop and Android apps (RiseupVPN, built on the Bitmask code) and a published JSON service configuration. Protocols: OpenVPN (AES-256-GCM) on every gateway. UDP: yes, on ports 53, 80 and 1194 in both TCP and UDP. Port forwarding: unverified: no page read states it. SOCKS5: unverified: no page read states a SOCKS5 endpoint. Obfuscation: obfs4 over TCP port 443 on every gateway. BitTorrent: the legacy help page lists p2p as a use the VPN supports; no current page states a rule.
tooling: The RiseupVPN app, or a plain OpenVPN client using the gateways, ports and cipher in the vendor's published service configuration (21 gateways, each with openvpn and obfs4 transports).
chaining: A free tunnel exit: traffic leaves from the address of one of 21 gateways, so the upstream sees a shared hosting-network address.

limits.value: 21 gateways, each a shared exit used by many users; the vendor asks for donations because capacity is funded by users ('approximately $60 USD per person per year')

limits_note: The pages read state no byte quota, device count or rate. The service has no account, so no per-account limit can be enforced by a login.
binding_note: No quota or rate is published and no account exists to enforce one; the open question is capacity (a donation-funded service with 21 gateways), which the limit vocabulary does not name.

identity_cost.detail: No account: 'no configuration, no account registration'. The vendor states it does not log the user's IP address. Donations are optional and go through Liberapay (card or Euro bank debit), PayPal or Bitcoin.

reliability_note: A donation-funded service run as 'an experiment to see if we can create a VPN service that is easy enough for everyone to use and that people will donate enough to sustain'; capacity and continuity depend on donations.
confidence_note: Documented for price, sign-up and the BitTorrent line; the protocol, UDP and obfuscation values are measured from the vendor's published service configuration (a probe of the JSON, status 200). The BitTorrent line comes from a legacy help page of unknown date, so it is the weakest value. Nothing was connected through the service.
price_per_tb_month: USD 0; a suggested donation of USD 60 a year; not a per-TB price
notes: Cheapest yearly price: USD 0 (donation-funded). The published service configuration lists 21 gateways, each offering OpenVPN on ports 53, 80 and 1194 over TCP and UDP and obfs4 on TCP 443.

evidence.proved: no account is needed to use RiseupVPN
